name: skillmcp
runtime: Claude Code, opencode, or any agent runtime that loads SKILL.md files
description: 50 validated skills for running a skills server over MCP stdio: wiring clients, designing tools, invoking them without wasting context, verifying the protocol, governing side effects and publishing packs.

skills.title: Stdio Client Config
skills.description: Wire a stdio MCP server into a client config so the agent can call it without a restart loop. Use when a skill or tool server exists on disk and the agent runtime needs a config entry for it

skills.title: Transport Choice
skills.description: Pick stdio or a network transport deliberately, based on where the server and its data actually live. Use when a new server is being designed and the transport decision is still open

skills.title: Protocol Version Handshake
skills.description: Negotiate the protocol revision explicitly and pin the one the server actually implements. Use when the client may run a different protocol revision than the server was written against

skills.title: Capability Negotiation Check
skills.description: Declare only the capabilities the server implements and refuse calls outside them. Use when the server exposes tools and the client must know whether to look for resources or prompts

skills.title: Server Discovery and Trust
skills.description: Decide which third-party tool servers to load by reading what they do before granting them a call surface. Use when an agent is about to be pointed at a server you did not write

skills.title: Local Versus Remote Boundary
skills.description: Keep a local file-reading server local, and state the trust boundary before anything crosses it. Use when a tool server could be exposed on a port to serve several agents

skills.title: Secrets Via Environment
skills.description: Pass credentials through the environment so they never appear in process arguments or config files. Use when a tool server needs a token to call an external service on the agent's behalf

skills.title: Restart and Reload Semantics
skills.description: Know what the server caches and what needs a restart, so stale data never masquerades as a bug. Use when packs or skills change on disk while a client session is running

skills.title: Tool Verb Naming
skills.description: Name tools after the action they perform so a model chooses correctly from the name alone. Use when a new tool is being added and the name is still free-form

skills.title: Input Schema Strictness
skills.description: Make the input schema the only place argument rules live, and refuse anything outside it. Use when a tool accepts structured arguments that a model will construct from context

skills.title: Bounded Output Design
skills.description: Cap every response so one tool call cannot fill an agent's context window. Use when a tool can return an unbounded list, a full file or a large body

skills.title: Error Shape For Agents
skills.description: Return errors an agent can act on: what failed, why, and the next call that would work. Use when a tool can fail because of bad arguments, missing files or an empty result

skills.title: Idempotency Annotation
skills.description: Mark which tools change state so a retry after a timeout cannot duplicate an action. Use when a tool writes to disk, sends a request or mutates a remote record

skills.title: Tool Surface Minimisation
skills.description: Ship the fewest tools that cover the workflow, because every extra tool is a wrong choice waiting to happen. Use when a server is accumulating tools and the list is getting hard for a model to choose from

skills.title: Destructive Tool Gating
skills.description: Require an explicit target and an explicit intent for any tool that deletes or overwrites. Use when a server exposes a tool that changes or removes data the agent did not create

skills.title: Description as Contract
skills.description: Write tool descriptions as the contract a model will follow, including what the tool does not do. Use when an agent must choose between tools without seeing the implementation

skills.title: Search Then Fetch Pattern
skills.description: Search first, fetch second, so context is spent on the one procedure that fits the task. Use when a corpus of skills or documents is larger than the context available for reading it

skills.title: Tool Call Budgeting
skills.description: Decide the call budget for a task before starting so an agent cannot loop on a tool. Use when an agent may retry or search repeatedly and each call costs context and latency

skills.title: Parallel Tool Call Safety
skills.description: Only parallelise calls that are independent, and never parallelise anything that writes. Use when several lookups are needed and latency matters

skills.title: Argument Construction From Artifacts
skills.description: Build tool arguments from captured artifacts rather than from memory, so ids and paths are exact. Use when a tool needs an identifier that already exists in a capture, report or file

skills.title: Tool Error Without Retry Storm
skills.description: Distinguish transient from deterministic tool failures so a retry cannot become a loop. Use when a tool call fails and the next action is still undecided

skills.title: Pagination and Limit Discipline
skills.description: Page through results deliberately and stop when the remaining results stop being useful. Use when a tool returns a truncated list with a total count

skills.title: Deterministic Command Choices
skills.description: Prefer commands whose output does not depend on locale, globbing or shell state. Use when an agent constructs commands that a shell will interpret before the tool sees them

skills.title: Context Window Management
skills.description: Spend context on the procedure you will follow, not on everything the server could return. Use when a session accumulates tool output and the budget for reasoning is shrinking

skills.title: Verify Tool Output Before Reporting
skills.description: Treat tool output as an observation to check, never as a conclusion to publish. Use when a tool result will be quoted in a report, ticket or decision

skills.title: Protocol Conformance Test
skills.description: Test the wire protocol directly, so a client bug and a server bug are distinguishable. Use when a client reports a failure and the server's own behaviour is unproven

skills.title: Lifecycle Test Initialize Then Tools
skills.description: Prove the handshake before the tool list, because a client never calls tools on a failed initialize. Use when a new server is being validated against a real client for the first time

skills.title: Tools List Schema Validation
skills.description: Validate every advertised schema as JSON Schema before a client tries to obey it. Use when a tool's input schema was edited and clients construct arguments from it

skills.title: Tool Call Error Paths
skills.description: Exercise each error path deliberately so a bad argument cannot produce a silent success. Use when a tool validates arguments and the failure branches are untested

skills.title: Fixture Driven Transcript Tests
skills.description: Keep a request/response transcript on disk and assert the server still matches it. Use when a protocol server has behaviours that must not drift across refactors

skills.title: Stdout Purity Check
skills.description: Assert that stdout carries only protocol messages, because one stray print breaks every client. Use when the server logs, warns or prints anything during normal operation

skills.title: Concurrency and Ordering Check
skills.description: Send several requests at once and confirm replies stay attributable and the server stays consistent. Use when the server indexes files or holds state that concurrent calls could race on

skills.title: Replay Transcript For Regression
skills.description: Re-run a stored session against a new build to catch protocol drift before a client does. Use when the server is about to be released and its wire behaviour must not change

skills.title: Scope Guard Before Execution
skills.description: Check the engagement scope before a tool touches a target, and refuse rather than warn. Use when a tool can act on arbitrary hosts and the agent may have the wrong target in context

skills.title: Rate Limit Respect
skills.description: Keep the server and its caller under whatever limits the target or host imposes. Use when tool calls cause outbound work, indexing scans or remote requests

skills.title: Credential Isolation
skills.description: Give the server its own credential scope so a compromised tool call cannot reach everything. Use when the server calls an upstream service on behalf of the agent

skills.title: Audit Log of Tool Calls
skills.description: Log every call with arguments and outcome so an agent's actions can be reconstructed. Use when the server can change state or reach anything outside its own directory

skills.title: Destructive Action Confirmation
skills.description: Require a second, explicit signal before a destructive call leaves a trace that cannot be undone. Use when the server exposes a tool whose effect cannot be reversed by the caller

skills.title: Data Retention Policy
skills.description: Decide how long tool inputs, outputs and logs live, and make deletion real rather than implied. Use when the server stores captures, findings or credentials-adjacent data

skills.title: Least Privilege Tool Grants
skills.description: Grant the agent only the tools it needs for the current task, not the whole server surface. Use when a client can restrict which tools an agent may call

skills.title: Third Party Server Sandboxing
skills.description: Run untrusted tool servers with the smallest filesystem and network reach that still works. Use when a server you did not write is part of the toolchain

skills.title: Human in the Loop Escalation
skills.description: Define the decisions an agent must hand back to a person instead of making alone. Use when an agent can act on systems where a wrong call is expensive or irreversible

skills.title: Skill Frontmatter Contract
skills.description: Keep the frontmatter fields identical across a pack so any loader can index it without special cases. Use when skills from several packs will be loaded by one runtime or one index

skills.title: One Procedure Per Skill
skills.description: Keep each skill to a single reproducible procedure so an agent can follow it without branching. Use when a skill has grown into a survey of several unrelated techniques

skills.title: When to Use and Avoid
skills.description: State both conditions so an agent can decline a skill that does not fit the target. Use when a skill is broad enough to be tempting in situations where it is wrong

skills.title: Signal and Pitfall Sections
skills.description: Write signals as observations and pitfalls as the mistakes that produce false findings. Use when a skill needs to help a reader decide mid-procedure whether they are on track

skills.title: Done When Criteria
skills.description: Define completion as observable artifacts so a skill cannot be declared finished on vibes. Use when a procedure has several steps and the endpoint of the work is ambiguous

skills.title: Reference Canonicalisation
skills.description: Cite canonical https references so a link keeps working after the pack is published. Use when a skill cites a specification, vendor document or research post

skills.title: Changelog and Versioning
skills.description: Version a pack so consumers know when a skill's meaning changed, not just its wording. Use when a pack is consumed by another project, an agent runtime or a pinned install

skills.title: Publishing a Pack Locally
skills.description: Lay out a pack so any skill-aware runtime recognises it without a bespoke loader. Use when a new skill pack is ready to be used by an agent runtime on the same machine
